name: EfficientNet-B0 face-manipulation detector (FaceForensics++ C23)
reason: Measured locally and rejected: the checkpoint scored the real Lenna face at 96% fake and an SBI-manipulated copy lower (86%) than the original — the signal is inverted/unusable for screening. See experiments/FACESWAP_EVALUATION.md. Use face-manipulation-vit-runtime.json instead.
limitations: Weights are not committed; run scripts/fetch_faceswap.py to download efficientnet_b0_ffpp_c23.pth (~17 MB) into models/.

Trained on FaceForensics++ C23 face crops — detects face manipulation (faceswap/reenactment), not full-scene generation; non-face images score unreliably and should be routed to the generator-detector members.
Publisher preprocessing is Resize(224)+ToTensor only — no ImageNet normalization; this profile sets mean=0/std=1 to match.

LICENSE: upstream marks this checkpoint 'research and educational purposes only — not intended for real-world forensic, biometric, surveillance, or law-enforcement applications'. Keep it an advisory ensemble member, never a standalone basis.
FaceForensics++ predates diffusion-era manipulation (2023+ neural filters may evade it); scores are a prioritization signal, not a truth label.
Third-party community checkpoint — cross-dataset accuracy beyond the publisher's FF++ claims is unverified; validate on local labeled data before trusting thresholds.
notes: Runtime 'torchvision' rebuilds efficientnet_b0 with a 2-class classifier tail (classifier[1]) and load_state_dict(strict=True).
Complements the generator-detector members: faceswap composites real pixels, which AIDE/UnivFD/CNNDetection structurally do not flag — this member covers the classic 'deepfake' manipulation family.
The checkpoint path is relative to this profile's directory (models/); keep it out of git — it is covered by .gitignore.
license: upstream community fine-tune — see source_url; FaceForensics++ data carries research-use terms
